name: Meyers Manx
hook: A surfer built this fibreglass beach buggy in his garage, then drove it the length of Baja faster than any motorcycle had.
story: April 1967. Bruce Meyers and Ted Mangels point a small fibreglass buggy north out of La Paz. The car is called Old Red, and Meyers made it himself in Newport Beach. He was a boat builder and a surfer, so he built the body the way he built boats: hand-laid fibreglass, curved and light, wrapped around Volkswagen Beetle parts. The record they are chasing belongs to motorcycles. Baja end to end, dirt and dust and cactus, with a Road & Track writer trailing them to see it done. They reach Tijuana in 34 hours and 45 minutes. That is more than five hours inside the old mark. Overnight, a beach toy is a serious off-road car. Six months later the first Mexican 1000 is run down the same peninsula, and a Manx wins that too, in 27 hours 38 minutes. Then a judge throws out Meyers's patent as unpatentable. Around 250,000 copies follow. He built about 6,000 of his own.
description: The Meyers Manx is a fibreglass dune buggy designed by Bruce Meyers in southern California. The first one, Old Red, was finished in 1964 with a load-bearing fibreglass body, and about a dozen were made that way. Later kits used a simpler tub bolted to a Volkswagen Beetle floorpan shortened by 14 and a quarter inches, with the Beetle's air-cooled flat-four behind the rear axle. B. F. Meyers & Co. built roughly 6,000 from 1964 to 1971.
